sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vāsudevaḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho yat tvā vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: Then Vāsudeva spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī: "Mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, hear what I am about to tell you."

sanskrit: upāramasva yuddhāya droṇād bharatasattama gṛdhyate hi sadā droṇo grahaṇe tava saṃyuge
english: "Withdraw from battle against Droṇa, O best of the Bhāratas, for Droṇa forever hungers to take you captive in the fray."

sanskrit: nānurūpam ahaṃ manye yuddham asya tvayā saha yo 'sya sṛṣṭo vināśāya sa enaṃ śvo haniṣyati
english: "I do not think this combat with him is fit for you; he who was born for his destruction shall slay him tomorrow."

sanskrit: parivarjya guruṃ yāhi yatra rājā suyodhanaḥ bhīmaś ca rathaśārdūlo yudhyate kauravaiḥ saha
english: "Avoid the preceptor and go to where King Suyodhana is, and where Bhīma, that tiger among chariot-warriors, fights against the Kauravas."

sanskrit: vāsudevavacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ muhūrtaṃ cintayitvā tu tato dāruṇam āhavam
english: Hearing the words of Vāsudeva, Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness, reflected for a moment upon that terrible battle.

sanskrit: prāyād drutam amitraghno yatra bhīmo vyavasthitaḥ vinighnaṃs tāvakān yodhān vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ
english: Then that slayer of foes swiftly set out for where Bhīma stood his ground, striking down your warriors like Death with jaws agape.

sanskrit: rathaghoṣeṇa mahatā nādayan vasudhātalam parjanya iva gharmānte nādayan vai diśo daśa
english: With the mighty thunder of his chariot he made the face of the earth resound, filling the ten directions with his roar like a rain-cloud at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: bhīmasya nighnataḥ śatrūn pārṣṇiṃ jagrāha pāṇḍavaḥ droṇo 'pi pāṇḍupāñcālān vyadhamad rajanīmukhe
english: The son of Pāṇḍu guarded the rear of Bhīma as he slew his enemies, while Droṇa too scattered the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas at the onset of night.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vartamāne tathā yuddhe ghorarūpe bhayāvahe tamasā saṃvṛte loke rajasā ca mahīpate nāpaśyanta raṇe yodhāḥ parasparam avasthitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As that battle, dreadful of form and fraught with terror, raged on, the world being veiled in darkness and in dust, O lord of the earth, the warriors stationed in the fray could not see one another.

sanskrit: anumānena saṃjñābhir yuddhaṃ tad vavṛte mahat naranāgāśvamathanaṃ paramaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: By guesswork and by signals that great combat was waged, a churning of men, elephants, and horses, supremely making the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇakṛpā vīrā bhīmapārṣatasātyakāḥ anyonyaṃ kṣobhayām āsuḥ sainyāni nṛpasattama
english: The heroes Droṇa, Karṇa, and Kṛpa, and Bhīma, the son of Pṛṣata, and Sātyaki threw each other's armies into turmoil, O best of kings.

sanskrit: vadhyamānāni sainyāni samantāt tair mahārathaiḥ tamasā rajasā caiva samantād vipradudruvuḥ
english: The armies, slaughtered on every side by those great chariot-warriors, fled in all directions, hemmed in by darkness and by dust.

sanskrit: te sarvato vidravanto yodhā vitrastacetasaḥ ahanyanta mahārāja dhāvamānāś ca saṃyuge
english: Those warriors, scattering in every direction with terror-stricken hearts, were cut down, O great king, even as they ran in the fray.

sanskrit: mahārathasahasrāṇi jaghnur anyonyam āhave andhe tamasi mūḍhāni putrasya tava mantrite
english: Thousands of great chariot-warriors slew one another in the fight, bewildered in the blind darkness, by the counsel of your son.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni senāgopāś ca bhārata vyamuhyanta raṇe tatra tamasā saṃvṛte sati
english: Then all the armies and the leaders of the host, O Bhārata, fell into confusion there in the battle, the field being shrouded in darkness.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca teṣāṃ saṃloḍyamānānāṃ pāṇḍavair nihataujasām andhe tamasi magnānām āsīt kā vo matis tadā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: As they were churned about by the Pāṇḍavas, their vigor struck down, sunk in blind darkness, what then was the resolve of your people?

sanskrit: kathaṃ prakāśas teṣāṃ vā mama sainyeṣu vā punaḥ babhūva loke tamasā tathā saṃjaya saṃvṛte
english: How, Saṃjaya, did light come again among them, or among my armies, when the world was so enveloped in darkness?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni hataśiṣṭāni yāni vai senāgoptṝn athādiśya punar vyūham akalpayat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then all the armies that survived the slaughter, appointing their commanders, formed up their battle-array once more.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ purastāj jaghane tu śalyas; tathā drauṇiḥ pārśvataḥ saubalaś ca svayaṃ tu sarvāṇi balāni rājan; rājābhyayād gopayan vai niśāyām
english: Droṇa stood in front, Śalya at the rear, while Droṇa's son and the son of Subala held the flanks; and the king himself, O king, moved forward in the night guarding all his forces.

sanskrit: uvāca sarvāṃś ca padātisaṃghān; duryodhanaḥ pārthiva sāntvapūrvam utsṛjya sarve paramāyudhāni; gṛhṇīta hastair jvalitān pradīpān
english: And Duryodhana, O prince, spoke gently to all the bands of foot-soldiers: "Lay aside your finest weapons, all of you, and take blazing lamps in your hands."

sanskrit: te coditāḥ pārthivasattamena; tataḥ prahṛṣṭā jagṛhuḥ pradīpān sā bhūya eva dhvajinī vibhaktā; vyarocatāgniprabhayā niśāyām
english: Urged on by that best of princes, they gladly took up the lamps; and the banner-bearing host, marshalled anew, shone with the light of fire in the night.

sanskrit: mahādhanair ābharaṇaiś ca divyaiḥ; śastraiḥ pradīptair abhisaṃpatadbhiḥ kṣaṇena sarve vihitāḥ pradīpā; vyadīpayaṃś ca dhvajinīṃ tadāśu
english: With costly and celestial ornaments, and with weapons flashing as they clashed together, the lamps arrayed in an instant straightway lit up the whole banner-bearing host.

sanskrit: sarvās tu senā vyatisevyamānāḥ; padātibhiḥ pāvakatailahastaiḥ prakāśyamānā dadṛśur niśāyāṃ; yathāntarikṣe jaladās taḍidbhiḥ
english: All the armies, attended on every hand by foot-soldiers bearing fire and oil, appeared, illumined in the night, like rain-clouds in the sky lit up by lightning.

sanskrit: prakāśitāyāṃ tu tathā dhvajinyāṃ; droṇo 'gnikalpaḥ pratapan samantāt rarāja rājendra suvarṇavarmā; madhyaṃ gataḥ sūrya ivāṃśumālī
english: When the host was thus illumined, Droṇa, blazing like fire and scorching all around, shone forth, O lord of kings, clad in golden mail, like the garlanded sun at its zenith.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadeṣv ābharaṇeṣu caiva; niṣkeṣu śuddheṣu śarāvareṣu pīteṣu śastreṣu ca pāvakasya; pratiprabhās tatra tato babhūvuḥ
english: Upon the ornaments of pure gold, the bright necklaces, the quivers, and the burnished weapons, the reflected radiance of the fire then played there.

sanskrit: gadāś ca śaikyāḥ parighāś ca śubhrā; ratheṣu śaktyaś ca vivartamānāḥ pratiprabhā raśmibhir ājamīḍha; punaḥ punaḥ saṃjanayanti dīptāḥ
english: The slung maces and gleaming iron clubs, and the spears whirling upon the chariots, O scion of Ajamīḍha, blazing, again and again kindled reflected gleams with their rays.

sanskrit: chatrāṇi bālavyajanānuṣaṅgā; dīptā maholkāś ca tathaiva rājan vyāghūrṇamānāś ca suvarṇamālā; vyāyacchatāṃ tatra tadā virejuḥ
english: The parasols and the trains of yak-tail fans, and the great blazing torches likewise, O king, and the golden garlands swaying upon the struggling warriors shone resplendent there.

sanskrit: śastraprabhābhiś ca virājamānaṃ; dīpaprabhābhiś ca tadā balaṃ tat prakāśitaṃ cābharaṇaprabhābhir; bhṛśaṃ prakāśaṃ nṛpate babhūva
english: Radiant with the gleam of weapons, and with the glow of the lamps, and lit up by the brightness of the ornaments, that host, O king, became exceedingly resplendent.

sanskrit: pītāni śastrāṇy asṛgukṣitāni; vīrāvadhūtāni tanudruhāṇi dīptāṃ prabhāṃ prājanayanta tatra; tapātyaye vidyud ivāntarikṣe
english: The burnished weapons, drenched with blood, brandished by the heroes and tearing into bodies, gave forth a flashing radiance there, like lightning in the sky at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: prakampitānām abhighātavegair; abhighnatāṃ cāpatatāṃ javena vaktrāṇy aśobhanta tadā narāṇāṃ; vāyvīritānīva mahāmbujāni
english: The faces of the men, shaken by the force of blows, striking and rushing in with speed, shone forth then like great lotuses stirred by the wind.

sanskrit: mahāvane dāva iva pradīpte; yathā prabhā bhāskarasyāpi naśyet tathā tavāsīd dhvajinī pradīptā; mahābhaye bhārata bhīmarūpā
english: As in a great forest ablaze with wildfire even the splendor of the sun would be lost, so blazed your banner-bearing host, O Bhārata, fearsome of form amid that great terror.

sanskrit: tat saṃpradīptaṃ balam asmadīyaṃ; niśāmya pārthās tvaritās tathaiva sarveṣu sainyeṣu padātisaṃghān; acodayaṃs te 'tha cakruḥ pradīpān
english: Beholding our host thus brightly ablaze, the sons of Pṛthā in like haste urged on the bands of foot-soldiers throughout all their armies, and they too made lamps.

sanskrit: gaje gaje sapta kṛtāḥ pradīpā; rathe rathe caiva daśa pradīpāḥ dvāv aśvapṛṣṭhe paripārśvato 'nye; dhvajeṣu cānye jaghaneṣu cānye
english: Seven lamps were set on each elephant, and ten lamps on each chariot, two upon every horse's back, and others at the flanks, others upon the standards, and others at the rear.

sanskrit: senāsu sarvāsu ca pārśvato 'nye; paścāt purastāc ca samantataś ca madhye tathānye jvalitāgnihastāḥ; senādvaye 'pi sma narā viceruḥ
english: And in all the armies others stood at the flanks, behind, in front, and all around; and others in the midst, with blazing fire in their hands, ranged through both the hosts.

sanskrit: sarveṣu sainyeṣu padātisaṃghā; vyāmiśritā hastirathāśvavṛndaiḥ madhye tathānye jvalitāgnihastā; vyadīpayan pāṇḍusutasya senām
english: Throughout all the armies the bands of foot-soldiers, mingled with the throngs of elephants, chariots, and horses, and others in the midst with blazing fire in their hands, lit up the host of the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tena pradīptena tathā pradīptaṃ; balaṃ tad āsīd balavad balena bhāḥ kurvatā bhānumatā graheṇa; divākareṇāgnir ivābhitaptaḥ
english: By that blazing host the other mighty host blazed in turn, as fire is kindled to a glow by the radiant, light-giving orb of the day-making sun.

sanskrit: tayoḥ prabhāḥ pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ; sarvā vyatikramya diśaś ca vṛddhāḥ tena prakāśena bhṛśaṃ prakāśaṃ; babhūva teṣāṃ tava caiva sainyam
english: The radiance of the two hosts, overspreading earth and sky, swelled across all the quarters; and by that brilliance their army and yours became exceedingly bright.

sanskrit: tena prakāśena divaṃgamena; saṃbodhitā devagaṇāś ca rājan gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṃghāḥ; samāgamann apsarasaś ca sarvāḥ
english: By that brilliance mounting to heaven the hosts of the gods were roused, O king, and the throngs of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and Siddhas, and all the Apsarases gathered there.

sanskrit: tad devagandharvasamākulaṃ ca; yakṣāsurendrāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiś ca hataiś ca vīrair divam āruhadbhir; āyodhanaṃ divyakalpaṃ babhūva
english: Thronged with gods and Gandharvas, with hosts of Yakṣas, lords of Asuras, and Apsarases, and with slain heroes ascending to heaven, that battlefield became like unto the celestial realm.

sanskrit: rathāśvanāgākuladīpadīptaṃ; saṃrabdhayodhāhatavidrutāśvam mahad balaṃ vyūḍharathāśvanāgaṃ; surāsuravyūhasamaṃ babhūva
english: Ablaze with lamps amid the press of chariots, horses, and elephants, its steeds driven in rout by furious warriors, that mighty host with its arrayed chariots, horses, and elephants became like the battle-array of gods and Asuras.

sanskrit: tac chaktisaṃghākulacaṇḍavātaṃ; mahārathābhraṃ rathavājighoṣam śastraughavarṣaṃ rudhirāmbudhāraṃ; niśi pravṛttaṃ naradevayuddham
english: With its fierce winds of massed spears, its clouds of great chariots, its thunder of cars and steeds, its downpour of weapon-floods and its streams of blood for rain, that battle of men and kings raged on through the night.

sanskrit: tasmin mahāgnipratimo mahātmā; saṃtāpayan pāṇḍavān vipramukhyaḥ gabhastibhir madhyagato yathārko; varṣātyaye tadvad abhūn narendra
english: In that field the great-souled chief of the twice-born, likened to a mighty fire, scorching the Pāṇḍavas, was as the sun risen to its zenith with its rays at the close of the rains, O lord of men.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prakāśite tathā loke rajasā ca tamovṛte samājagmur atho vīrāḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the world was thus illumined, yet shrouded in dust and darkness, the heroes came together, each seeking the destruction of the other.

sanskrit: te sametya raṇe rājañ śastraprāsāsidhāriṇaḥ parasparam udaikṣanta parasparakṛtāgasaḥ
english: Meeting in battle, O king, bearing weapons, lances, and swords, they glared at one another, each having wronged the other.

sanskrit: pradīpānāṃ sahasraiś ca dīpyamānaiḥ samantataḥ virarāja tadā bhūmir dyaur grahair iva bhārata
english: With thousands of lamps blazing on every side, the earth then shone, O Bhārata, like the sky bright with its planets.

sanskrit: ulkāśataiḥ prajvalitai raṇabhūmir vyarājata dahyamāneva lokānām abhāve vai vasuṃdharā
english: With hundreds of blazing torches the battlefield shone resplendent, as the earth would seem to burn at the dissolution of the worlds.

sanskrit: prādīpyanta diśaḥ sarvāḥ pradīpais taiḥ samantataḥ varṣāpradoṣe khadyotair vṛtā vṛkṣā ivābabhuḥ
english: All the quarters were lit up by those lamps on every side; they shone like trees beset with fireflies in the early dusk of the rains.

sanskrit: asajjanta tato vīrā vīreṣv eva pṛthak pṛthak nāgā nāgaiḥ samājagmus turagāḥ saha vājibhiḥ
english: Then the heroes engaged hero against hero, each apart; elephants closed with elephants, and steeds met with steeds.

sanskrit: rathā rathavarair eva samājagmur mudānvitāḥ tasmin rātrimukhe ghore putrasya tava śāsanāt
english: Chariots met with the foremost of chariots, filled with eager joy, in that dread onset of night, by the command of your son.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahārāja kauravāṇām anīkinīm vyadhamat tvarayā yuktaḥ kṣapayan sarvapārthivān
english: Then Arjuna, O great king, scattered the host of the Kauravas, applying himself with speed and destroying all the princes.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasmin praviṣṭe saṃrabdhe mama putrasya vāhinīm amṛṣyamāṇe durdharṣe kiṃ va āsīn manas tadā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that furious and unbearable one, the unassailable, had broken into my son's army, what then was the resolve of your people?

sanskrit: kim amanyanta sainyāni praviṣṭe śatrutāpane duryodhanaś ca kiṃ kṛtyaṃ prāptakālam amanyata
english: What did the armies think when that scorcher of foes broke in, and what fitting deed did Duryodhana judge the hour to require?

sanskrit: ke cainaṃ samare vīraṃ pratyudyayur ariṃdamam ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ ke ca droṇasya savyataḥ
english: Who went forth against that hero, that tamer of foes, in the fight? Who guarded the right wheel of Droṇa's car, and who the left?

sanskrit: ke pṛṣṭhato 'sya hy abhavan vīrā vīrasya yudhyataḥ ke purastād agacchanta nighnataḥ śātravān raṇe
english: What heroes stood at the back of that hero as he fought, and who advanced before him as he slew his enemies in battle?

sanskrit: yat prāviśan maheṣvāsaḥ pāñcālān aparājitaḥ nṛtyann iva naravyāghro rathamārgeṣu vīryavān
english: When that mighty bowman, unconquered, broke into the Pāñcālas, that tiger among men, valiant, seeming to dance along the chariot-paths—

sanskrit: dadāha ca śarair droṇaḥ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajān dhūmaketur iva kruddhaḥ sa kathaṃ mṛtyum īyivān
english: and Droṇa burned with his shafts the ranks of Pāñcāla chariots, like wrathful fire whose banner is smoke—how then did he come to his death?

sanskrit: avyagrān eva hi parān kathayasy aparājitān hatāṃś caiva viṣaṇṇāṃś ca viprakīrṇāṃś ca śaṃsasi rathino virathāṃś caiva kṛtān yuddheṣu māmakān
english: You tell of the foes as unflustered and unvanquished, yet you report mine as slain, despondent, and scattered, my chariot-warriors stripped of their cars in the battles.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca droṇasya matam ājñāya yoddhukāmasya tāṃ niśām duryodhano mahārāja vaśyān bhrātṝn abhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: Perceiving the intent of Droṇa, who wished to fight on through that night, Duryodhana, O great king, addressed his obedient brothers.

sanskrit: vikarṇaṃ citrasenaṃ ca mahābāhuṃ ca kauravam durdharṣaṃ dīrghabāhuṃ ca ye ca teṣāṃ padānugāḥ
english: Vikarṇa and Citrasena, and the mighty-armed Kaurava, the unassailable long-armed one, and those who followed at their heels—

sanskrit: droṇaṃ yattāḥ parākrāntāḥ sarve rakṣata pṛṣṭhataḥ hārdikyo dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ śalyaś caivottaraṃ tathā
english: "Strive valiantly, all of you, and guard Droṇa from behind; let the son of Hṛdika guard the right wheel and Śalya likewise the left."

sanskrit: trigartānāṃ ca ye śūrā hataśiṣṭā mahārathāḥ tāṃś caiva sarvān putras te samacodayad agrataḥ
english: And those valiant great chariot-warriors of the Trigartas who had survived the slaughter—all of them your son urged forward to the van.

sanskrit: ācāryo hi susaṃyatto bhṛśaṃ yattāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ taṃ rakṣata susaṃyattā nighnantaṃ śātravān raṇe
english: "The preceptor is well girt for battle, and the Pāṇḍavas strive hard; guard him, then, well prepared, as he slays his enemies in the fray."

sanskrit: droṇo hi balavān yuddhe kṣiprahastaḥ parākramī nirjayet tridaśān yuddhe kim u pārthān sasomakān
english: "For Droṇa is mighty in battle, quick of hand and full of valor; he could vanquish even the thirty gods in fight—how much more the sons of Pṛthā with the Somakas."

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ sahitāḥ sarve bhṛśaṃ yattā mahārathāḥ droṇaṃ rakṣata pāñcālyād dhṛṣṭadyumnān mahārathāt
english: "Therefore do you all, united and striving hard, O great chariot-warriors, guard Droṇa from the Pāñcāla prince Dhṛṣṭadyumna, that great car-warrior."

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveyeṣu sainyeṣu yodhaṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ na tam yo jayeta raṇe droṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnād ṛte nṛpāḥ
english: "Among the armies of the Pāṇḍavas I see no warrior, O kings, who could conquer Droṇa in battle, save Dhṛṣṭadyumna alone."

sanskrit: tasya sarvātmanā manye bhāradvājasya rakṣaṇam sa guptaḥ somakān hanyāt sṛñjayāṃś ca sarājakān
english: "Therefore I deem it best to guard the son of Bharadvāja with all our might; protected, he will slay the Somakas and the Sṛñjayas together with their kings."

sanskrit: sṛñjayeṣv atha sarveṣu nihateṣu camūmukhe dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ raṇe drauṇir nāśayiṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: "And when all the Sṛñjayas are slain at the head of the host, Droṇa's son will destroy Dhṛṣṭadyumna in battle, beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: tathārjunaṃ raṇe karṇo vijeṣyati mahārathaḥ bhīmasenam ahaṃ cāpi yuddhe jeṣyāmi daṃśitaḥ
english: "So too will Karṇa, that great chariot-warrior, conquer Arjuna in battle; and I myself, clad in mail, shall vanquish Bhīmasena in the fight."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mama jayo vyaktaṃ dīrghakālaṃ bhaviṣyati tasmād rakṣata saṃgrāme droṇam eva mahārathāḥ
english: "Plainly, then, victory shall be mine for ages to come; therefore guard Droṇa in the battle, O great chariot-warriors."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bharataśreṣṭha putro duryodhanas tava vyādideśa tataḥ sainyaṃ tasmiṃs tamasi dāruṇe
english: Having spoken thus, O best of the Bhāratas, your son Duryodhana then drew up the army in that terrible darkness.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ rātrau tad bharatarṣabha ubhayoḥ senayor ghoraṃ vijayaṃ prati kāṅkṣiṇoḥ
english: Then that dread battle was waged by night, O bull of the Bhāratas, between the two armies, each longing for victory.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ kauravaṃ sainyam arjunaṃ cāpi kauravāḥ nānāśastrasamāvāpair anyonyaṃ paryapīḍayan
english: Arjuna pressed hard upon the Kaurava host, and the Kauravas upon Arjuna; with showers of varied weapons they tormented one another.

sanskrit: drauṇiḥ pāñcālarājānaṃ bhāradvājaś ca sṛñjayān chādayām āsatuḥ saṃkhye śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Droṇa's son covered the king of the Pāñcālas, and the son of Bharadvāja the Sṛñjayas, in the fray, with their straight-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: pāṇḍupāñcālasenānāṃ kauravāṇāṃ ca māriṣa āsīn niṣṭānako ghoro nighnatām itaretaram
english: Of the armies of the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas, and of the Kauravas, O venerable one, there arose a dreadful din as they struck one another down.

sanskrit: naivāsmābhir na pūrvair no dṛṣṭaṃ pūrvaṃ tathāvidham yuddhaṃ yādṛśam evāsīt tāṃ rātriṃ sumahābhayam
english: Never by us, nor by those before us, was such a thing seen before as that battle which raged that night, fraught with the greatest terror.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vartamāne tathā raudre rātriyuddhe viśāṃ pate sarvabhūtakṣayakare dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As that fierce night-battle, the destroyer of all beings, raged on, O lord of peoples, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma,

sanskrit: abravīt pāṇḍavāṃś caiva pāñcālāṃś ca sasomakān abhyadravata gacchadhvaṃ droṇam eva jighāṃsayā
english: spoke to the Pāṇḍavas and to the Pāñcālas with the Somakas: "Charge forward, go against Droṇa himself with intent to slay."

sanskrit: rājñas te vacanād rājan pāñcālāḥ somakās tathā droṇam evābhyavartanta nadanto bhairavān ravān
english: At the word of your king, O king, the Pāñcālas and the Somakas alike bore down upon Droṇa, uttering fearful roars.

sanskrit: tān vayaṃ pratigarjantaḥ pratyudyātās tv amarṣitāḥ yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ yathāsattvaṃ ca saṃyuge
english: We, roaring back at them and burning with wrath, went forth against them in the fray to the utmost of our power, our zeal, and our strength.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyo yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat droṇaṃ prati jighāṃsantaṃ matto mattam iva dvipam
english: And Kṛtavarman, the son of Hṛdika, rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira, who sought to slay Droṇa, as one rutting elephant charges another.
